To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transcription of the hsp genes is modulated by pH in a PacC-dependent manner.
the hsp70 gene expression in the N. cransa fungus is modulated in a complex fashion by extracellular pH and phosphate concentration.
the N. crassa hsp70 genes are differentially regulated by pH changes and heat shock.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the hsp genes in response to changes in environmental conditions, such as pH, phosphate concentration, and temperature.
the identification of genes that are differentially expressed in response to extrinsic stimuli.
the regulation of the expression of hsp70 genes in N. crassa and the role of the pacC and nuc-1 genes in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N. crassa heat shock genes are differentially regulated by extracellular pH and phosphate availability.
the N. crassa hsp70 genes are regulated in response to extrinsic and intrinsic signals.
the expression of the N. cransa hsp70- genes is regulated in response to the environmental changes that occur during the life of the organism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hsp70- 1 and hsp 70-2 genes are regulated by PacC in response to extracelluar pH changes, and hsp 7 0-3 gene is regulated by NUC-1 in response to phosphate availability.
the hsp70 gene family is modulated by the pH of the extracellular environment, the phosphate concentration, and the temperature.
the hsp70 genes are regulated by the pH and heat shock response pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heat shock and extracellular pH sensing pathways are integrated at the transcriptional level.
the transcription of hsp genes is modulated by the extracellular pH and by the phosphate availability in the growth medium.
the transcriptional regulation of the three hsp70 genes is modulated by extracellular pH changes and by the availability of phosphate.
